deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss records the dimensions of the telescope of his Repsold circle. Repsold's meridian circle came to the Göttingen observatory around 1818; the previous page is dated May 1822. He uses them to compute the magnifications of its three two-lens eyepieces. The next page continues with the matrix (α, β, γ, δ) description of the same lens system.

(A) Objective focal length.
- Total tube length with eyepiece no. 2 pushed fully in: 2.436 m.
- Minus the ring (Kranz) of the eyepiece, 0.003 m, gives the tube without the eyepiece tube: L = 2.433 m.
- The crosshairs (Fäden) sit 0.024 m from the eyepiece end.
- The outer face of the objective sits 0.097 m from the other end.
- So the crosshair-to-outer-face distance is 2.433 − 0.024 − 0.097 = 2.312 m.
- Subtracting the whole objective thickness, about 0.124 m, gives the objective focal length a = 2.188 m.
- Converted to Paris feet (1 pied = 0.324839 m): 2.188/0.324839 ≈ 6.736, which Gauss writes as 6.737 pieds.

(B) Eyepieces 1, 2, 3 (all in mm).
- For each eyepiece he lists the distance of the first (field) lens from the front ring, its aperture and its focal length c.
- He lists the same three quantities for the second lens, whose focal length is b.
- The row labelled q is the separation of the two lenses, q = d2 − d1 (my identification, confirmed numerically):
  - 23.80 − 4.15 = 19.65
  - 20.70 − 3.45 = 17.25
  - 26.00 − 5.20 = 20.80
- The thin-lens combination of focal lengths c and b at separation q has equivalent focal length F = bc/(b + c − q). (The derivation is mine; it is implicit on the page and made explicit on the next page through the coefficients α'' = −bc/(a(b+c−q)) and δ'' = −a(b+c−q)/(bc).)
- The telescope magnification is therefore m = a/F. Gauss writes it as m = a(q − c − b)/(bc), which is negative, signalling the inverted image; the absolute values tabulated are:
  - Eyepiece 1: 2188·43.18/(32.06·30.77) = 95.77
  - Eyepiece 2: 2188·58.99/(31.45·44.79) = 91.63
  - Eyepiece 3: 2188·64.80/(43.95·41.65) = 77.455, recorded as 77.46.
- The next page uses the same system to get the eye distance (exit pupil position), c(b−q)/(b+c−q) + a/m², and the field sizes.
errors: No substantive arithmetic errors; all subtractions and all three magnifications check out.
Sign: the formula a(q−c−b)/(bc) gives negative values (inverted image), but the tabulated values are absolute values. This is a convention, not an error.

Taking the focal length as the crosshair-to-outer-face distance minus the full objective thickness is a rough approximation (Gauss marks the thickness 'cca'). The true focal length is measured from the rear principal plane of a thick doublet, so a is uncertain at the mm–cm level.

Paris-foot conversion: 2.188 m corresponds to 6.7357 pieds; 6.737 corresponds to 2.1884 m. This is a slight rounding difference, possibly reflecting an unrounded a or a slightly different toise value.
Eyepiece 3: the exact value is 77.455, which Gauss rounds up to 77.46. This is acceptable.

results.what: Equivalent focal length of two thin lenses (focal lengths b, c, separation q): F = bc/(b+c−q), and the telescope magnification m = a/F = a(b+c−q)/(bc)
results.modern_name: Combination formula for two thin lenses (Gullstrand-type equivalent power); telescope angular magnification

results.what: Practical determination of the objective focal length from measured tube dimensions and conversion to Paris feet
Implicit use (made explicit on the next page) of linear transfer coefficients for the lens system

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine instrument calibration: tube measurements and eyepiece magnifications via the standard two-lens formula. It is of mild biographical interest because the companion page shows Gauss already using linear transfer coefficients around 1822, about two decades before Dioptrische Untersuchungen. However, his long-standing interest in dioptrics is known.

checkable.asserts: equals 0: equivalent focal length of two thin lenses

transcription_corrections: 'Fäden vom Ocularende 0,024[?]': 0,024 is confirmed by the arithmetic 2.433−0.024−0.097 = 2.312.
'Brennweite des Obj 2,188[?]': 2,188 is confirmed (2.312−0.124); in the image an earlier digit appears to be overwritten with 8.
'4,15[?]', '3,45[?]', '23,80[?]', '20,80[?]' are all confirmed by q = d2 − d1 and the magnification checks (23.80 is overwritten from 22.80; 20,80 is overwritten).
The label 'q' belongs to the row 19.65/17.25/20.80, which is the lens separation, not a magnification. The row 95.77/91.63/77.46 contains the magnifications m.
The first lens's focal length is labelled 'c' (written as a large C/c in the margin) and the second lens's 'b'.
